findings.description: Critical: D13 assigns reverse enforcement ownership to the capability at openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/design.md D13 lines 429-468 and spec lines 202-217, but openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/contracts/traceability-exclusions.schema.json lines 18-22 explicitly permits cross-capability requirement exclusions. That lets a file under capability A excuse capability B's requirement, creating a state B cannot own: B may be reverse-enforced while A suppresses its gap, or B may be not opted in while A's file changes B's reported completeness.
findings.resolution: Constrain requirement exclusions to the capability named by the containing traceability-exclusions.yaml file, or add an explicit cited-capability acknowledgement artifact and scenarios defining who owns cross-capability exclusions and which capability's reverse opt-in they affect.

findings.description: Critical: D12 claims the full sweep can block merges while specifying CI on main as push-triggered at openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/design.md lines 363-366, and task 5.7 repeats that at tasks.md lines 493-498. A push event on main runs after a merge has already landed, so it can red main but cannot block the merge it is meant to guard.
findings.resolution: Specify the full sweep as a required pull_request/merge_group check for merge blocking, optionally also running on push to main as a post-merge sweep; update task 5.7 and the acceptance wording so 'blocking' maps to an actually pre-merge CI context.

findings.description: Critical: wp-wiring's dispatch precondition is only prose at openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/work-packages.yaml lines 384-390, while the machine-readable depends_on list at lines 394-396 includes only wp-gate and wp-matrix. The scheduler can dispatch wp-wiring before human tasks 4.1, 4.2, 4.2b, and 5.2 land, making the real-artifact RED demonstrations impossible or fixture-only despite the plan saying that is invalid.
findings.resolution: Represent the human artifacts as machine-readable dependencies or checkpoints, or split wp-wiring into an early wiring package and a later demonstration package that depends on explicit human-completed artifacts.

findings.description: Critical: The malformed-input requirement at openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md lines 474-520 covers malformed contracts and traceability blocks, but not malformed, empty, schema-invalid, or unreadable traceability-exclusions.yaml files. D13 makes that file's existence the reverse opt-in switch, so an unreadable or unparsable switch artifact must fail closed rather than being treated as absent, empty, or reporting-only; task 3.4 at tasks.md lines 225-236 also lacks that RED case.
findings.resolution: Add a scenario and task coverage requiring a present-but-empty YAML file, malformed YAML, schema-invalid exclusions shape, and unreadable exclusions file to exit non-zero naming the file; only a valid empty list should mean 'opted in with no exclusions'.

findings.description: The wp-model refutation is supported by the repository evidence: generate_contract_schemas.py renders InterfaceDescriptor only at packages/gen-eval/scripts/generate_contract_schemas.py lines 80-90; InterfaceDescriptor reaches ServiceSpec/EndpointSpec/McpToolSpec/CommandSpec at descriptor.py lines 191-271, not FlagSpec/PositionalSpec/ToolCommandSpec or service_descriptor.OperationSpec. generate_tool_descriptor.py uses exclude_defaults=True on command, flag, and positional payloads at lines 118-137, so an optional traceability field with default None should not drift evaluation/descriptor.yaml until real traceability blocks are added and the human retrofit regenerates it.
findings.resolution: Keep wp-model's generated-artifact write scope narrow, but preserve the existing descriptor_identity verification step so this assumption is continuously checked.
